swap: Same structure, bodyweight burst (burpees or squat jumps) instead of equipment
how_to_perform: Go hard for 15-20s, then immediately move into the anti-extension hold — test whether the brace holds when you're blowing, not fresh.
cue: Your stance doesn't get a rest just because you're tired. Hold it anyway.

name: Impact-Grip Endurance
focus: Trains forearm and grip endurance under repeated rhythmic impact — the cumulative demand on the hands across a long innings of bat-to-ball contact.
execution: Repeated Hammer Strikes on a Tire (rhythmic impact) + Sustained Towel/Rope Grip Hold
swap: Repeated Band-Resisted Chop Strikes (same rhythm) + Sustained Towel Grip Hold
muscles: forearm flexors/extensors, grip muscles, wrist stabilizers
how_to_perform: Rhythmic hammer strikes onto a tire or heavy bag — real repeated impact through the grip. Immediately into a sustained hold (towel or thick rope) to fatigue grip endurance right after.
cue: Your hands take hundreds of hits in an innings. Build hands that don't give up late.
guidance: 15-20 strikes per side, into 20-30s grip hold, 2-3 rounds

name: Internal Rotation Range Primer
focus: Trains the hip internal-rotation range that the database's powerful rotational complexes assume is already available — the mobility prerequisite behind safe, full rotational power.
execution: 90/90 Hip Switch with Loaded Internal Rotation Press (light plate on the front shin through the rotation)
swap: Bodyweight 90/90 Hip Switch, same pattern, no load
muscles: deep hip rotators, glute med/min, adductors
how_to_perform: Seated 90/90, rotate smoothly between sides keeping both knees down. Light plate pressed into the front shin adds resistance through the internal rotation range.
cue: This is the mobility that makes your powerful rotation safe. Own the range before you load the speed.
guidance: 6-8 controlled switches per side, slow tempo

name: Visual Drop Reaction Step
focus: Trains footwork initiated by a visual stimulus alone, with no verbal call — closer to how a batting decision is actually triggered than the database's existing audio-cued reactive drills.
execution: Partner Ball Drop (varied height/zone) + Reactive Step to Catch Before Second Bounce
swap: Self-Thrown Tennis Ball Against a Wall + Reactive Step to Catch on Rebound
muscles: whole-body reactive — glutes, quads, calves (first-step initiation), visual-motor coordination
how_to_perform: Partner drops a ball without warning, varying the zone. Athlete reacts purely to the visual drop, no call given, stepping to catch before the second bounce.
cue: React to what you see, not what you hear. Nobody calls out a short ball.
guidance: 6-8 reps, varied direction, full reset between each

name: High Reach Stabilization
focus: Trains stabilizing a high, exposed single-arm position under light load — the vertical plane of movement the rest of the database (lateral, rotational, forward/back) doesn't touch.
execution: Single-Arm Overhead Reach-and-Hold (light Dumbbell) from a Split-Stance Base, 2-3s hold at full reach
swap: Single-Arm Overhead Band Reach-and-Hold, same base
muscles: shoulder stabilizers (rotator cuff), serratus anterior, obliques (contralateral stabilization), lats
how_to_perform: Split stance for a stable base, reach one arm fully overhead with light load, hold at full extension before a controlled return.
cue: Get tall and still at the top — don't just reach, hold the position.
guidance: 4-5 reps per side, 2-3s hold each, controlled tempo
